item: Row 410-A: an import never keeps its incoming corpus on disk in plaintext (R829 A)
summary: Every restore or import wrote a full plaintext copy of the incoming corpus into its staging folder and kept it for the whole merge (hours on a large backup). A1: an encrypted volume-set member is no longer exported to plaintext; it is read in place under the passphrase that opens it (one full rewrite of the incoming corpus and half the staging disk saved). A2: every other path (zip and OOENC1 uploads, bare SQLite and legacy .ooenc, legacy volume sets, a corpus not encrypted in its backup, and the custody log) is sealed as soon as its checks pass into a SQLCipher copy under a random 256-bit key held only in this process, never written or derived from a passphrase; the plaintext is unlinked. Keys reach SQLite only through set_key or a bound ATTACH ... KEY ? with no statement trace watching (a trace expands bound values: measured). Staged connections run trusted_schema off and cell_size_check on, and a trigger, view or virtual table the app does not make is refused before any row is read. A damaged corpus that cannot be read in full is refused at staging, before the merge. The merge gives a keyed inc its own cache. Proof run numbers in the PR. No schema change, no version bump.
